summary: This regulation explains the rules for related party transactions by certain listed entities with non-convertible securities. It requires these companies to follow general transaction rules, obtain specific approvals, and make disclosures. Certain kinds of transactions and older debt securities have exceptions.
points: The listed entity must follow the general related party transaction provisions except for specific sub-regulations.
The listed entity must get a prior No-Objection Certificate from the Debenture Trustee for material transactions and modifications.
The Debenture Trustee must obtain approval from unrelated debenture holders holding more than fifty percent in value.
The listed entity must obtain shareholder approval through a resolution after getting the debenture holder approval.
The listed entity must submit disclosures of related party transactions to the stock exchanges and publish them on its website.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited, a heavy value debt listed entity, planned a material transaction with a related party. First, the audit committee defined the material modification. Next, Meera Textiles requested a prior No-Objection Certificate from the Debenture Trustee. The Debenture Trustee then collected votes from unrelated debenture holders holding more than fifty percent in value. Once those debenture holders approved, Meera Textiles sought the approval of the shareholders through a resolution. Finally, Meera Textiles submitted the required disclosures to the stock exchanges and published them on its website along with its standalone financial results for the half year.

terms.meaning: An entity that protects the interests of debenture holders
Business deals between a company and its connected persons or affiliates
A formal decision passed by shareholders or members

watch: Make sure not to assume penalties or deadlines that are not explicitly stated in the text.
